title: "Svelte SDK"
description: "@seamless-auth/svelte adds Seamless Auth to a Svelte 5 application: a rune-based session, SvelteKit load guards, and optional sign-in screens."
sidebar:

---

`@seamless-auth/svelte` is the official Svelte integration for Seamless Auth. It gives a Svelte 5
application the same session state, auth actions, and optional sign-in screens the
[React SDK](/build/react-sdk) gives a React app, in Svelte's own idioms: a session whose properties
are runes, Svelte context to share it, and SvelteKit `load` functions as guards.

It is a thin binding over `@seamless-auth/client`, the framework-free core the React, React Native,
[Angular](/build/angular-sdk), and [Vue](/build/vue-sdk) SDKs also build on, so sign-in behaves the
same in every binding. The Svelte screens keep the React screens' accessible names, and
`seamless verify` runs the same browser specs against both.

---

## How It Fits

```txt
Svelte app (browser)
  -> your backend's /auth adapter routes, with signed httpOnly cookies
  -> Seamless Auth API
```

The browser model is the same as React's: the [server adapter](/build/server-sdks) keeps the auth
API's tokens and the browser holds only `httpOnly` cookies on your domain. The Svelte SDK has no
bearer mode. Its configuration has no transport option, so no token can reach page scripts, and
nothing it writes to browser storage is a credential. See
[Cookie, Session, And Token Reference](/reference/cookies-sessions-tokens).

---

## Requirements

- Svelte 5
- For the guards and the SvelteKit navigator in `@seamless-auth/svelte/kit`: SvelteKit 2.26 or later,
  or SvelteKit 3. The root entry works in any Svelte 5 application
- A backend mounting the Seamless Auth adapter routes at `/auth`, for example `@seamless-auth/express`

---

## Installation

```bash
npm install @seamless-auth/svelte
```

`@seamless-auth/client` comes with it.

---

## Configure A SvelteKit Application

The examples import from `$lib`, as SvelteKit 2 does. SvelteKit 3 renamed it to `#lib`.

Create the session once:

```ts
// src/lib/auth.ts
import { createSeamlessAuth } from '@seamless-auth/svelte'

export const auth = createSeamlessAuth({ apiHost: 'https://app.example.com' })
```

The session lives in the browser, so render the application there. A backend-for-frontend app usually
ships as a single-page app (`adapter-static` with a fallback page):

```ts
// src/routes/+layout.ts
export const ssr = false
```

Hand the session and a navigator to everything below the root layout:

```svelte
<!-- src/routes/+layout.svelte -->
<script lang="ts">
  import { setAuthNavigator, setSeamlessAuth } from '@seamless-auth/svelte'
  import { createKitNavigator } from '@seamless-auth/svelte/kit'
  import { auth } from '$lib/auth'

  let { children } = $props()

  setSeamlessAuth(auth)
  setAuthNavigator(createKitNavigator(auth))
</script>

{@render children()}
```

| Option                     | Default          | Purpose                                                              |
| -------------------------- | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `apiHost`                  | required         | Origin of the server adapter                                         |
| `basePath`                 | `/auth`          | Where the adapter is mounted on `apiHost`                            |
| `magicLinkRedirectUri`     | the deployment's | Where an emailed magic link lands                                    |
| `autoDetectPreviousSignIn` | `true`           | Open the login screen on Sign In for a browser that signed in before |
| `initialSession`           | none             | A session your server already resolved                               |
| `ports`                    | browser          | `passkeys` and `oauthRedirect` ports                                 |
| `fetch`                    | global `fetch`   | The fetch auth requests go through                                   |
| `trustedOrigins`           | none             | Other origins of yours that may receive the session cookies          |
| `injectStyles`             | `true`           | Whether the built-in screens add their stylesheet to the page        |
| `cspNonce`                 | none             | A CSP nonce for that stylesheet                                      |
| `signedInPath`             | `/`              | Where the built-in screens go after sign-in                          |
| `loginPath`                | `/login`         | Where `requireAuth` sends someone who is signed out                  |

---

## Guards

Guard a route with a `load` function:

```ts
// src/routes/(app)/+layout.ts
import { requireAuth } from '@seamless-auth/svelte/kit'
import { auth } from '$lib/auth'

export const load = requireAuth(auth)
```

| Guard                          | Admits                                    | Otherwise                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `requireAuth(auth, options?)`  | A signed-in user, with `roles` when given | Redirects to `redirectTo` (default `loginPath`), or `forbiddenRedirectTo` (default `signedInPath`) for a missing role |
| `requireGuest(auth, options?)` | Someone signed out                        | Redirects to `redirectTo` (default `signedInPath`)                                                           |

They wait for the session to be read before deciding, so reloading a protected page does not bounce a
signed-in user to the login screen. They run again on every navigation and whenever the session
changes (a sign-out in another tab, an expired session, a switched organization), as long as the
navigator from `createKitNavigator` is set in the root layout. A server render that was not handed an
`initialSession` cannot see the session, so `requireAuth` treats it as signed out and redirects.

`roles` uses the same matching as the auth API, scoped roles such as `org:admin` included. A guard
decides what to render; it is not access control. Your backend still checks every request with
`requireAuth`. See [Secure Routes](/build/secure-routes).

Put `requireGuest` only on the screens that start a sign-in (`login`, `passkey-login`,
`magic-link-sent`). A user can already have a session when `register-passkey`, `oauth/callback`, or
`verify-magiclink` renders.

---

## Reading Session State

Every property of the session is reactive, so read it straight in markup or an `$effect`:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { goto } from '$app/navigation'
  import { getSeamlessAuth } from '@seamless-auth/svelte'

  const auth = getSeamlessAuth()

  async function signOut() {
    await auth.logout()
    await goto('/login')
  }
</script>

{#if auth.user}
  <span>{auth.user.email}</span>
  <button type="button" onclick={signOut}>Logout</button>
{/if}
```

- **Properties:** `state`, `user`, `isAuthenticated`, `loading`, `credentials`, `organizations`,
  `activeOrganization`, `stepUpStatus`, `hasSignedInBefore`, plus `loginMethods`,
  `loginMethodsLoading`, `passkeySupported`, and `passkeySupportLoading`.
- **Actions:** `login`, `handlePasskeyLogin`, `registerPasskey`, `refreshSession`, `logout`,
  `logoutAllSessions`, `deleteUser`, `updateCredential`, `deleteCredential`, `switchOrganization`,
  `listOAuthProviders`, `startOAuthLogin`, `finishOAuthLogin`, `refreshStepUpStatus`,
  `verifyStepUpWithPasskey`, `verifyStepUpWithPasskeyPrf`, and `verifyStepUpWithTotp`.
- **Also:** `hasRole`, `hasScopedRole`, `markSignedIn`, `whenSettled()`, `loadLoginMethods()` and
  `checkPasskeySupport()` (each read once and cached), `authorizedFetch`, `client` (the headless
  client for OTP, magic link, organization, and TOTP calls), `ports`, and `destroy()`.

Every request action resolves to a `SeamlessAuthResult<T>`, `{ data, error }`, and does not throw
for an HTTP or network failure, the same convention as the React SDK. `authorizedFetch` sends the
session only to `apiHost` and `trustedOrigins`; see
[Calling Your Own API](/build/react-sdk#calling-your-own-api).

---

## Built-In Screens

A SvelteKit library cannot add routes to your application, so mount each screen in its own
`+page.svelte`:

```svelte
<!-- src/routes/login/+page.svelte -->
<script lang="ts">
  import { SaLogin } from '@seamless-auth/svelte'
</script>

<SaLogin />
```

| Default path        | Component                     | Purpose                                                     |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/login`            | `SaLogin`                     | Sign in with an email or phone number, or create an account |
| `/passkey-login`    | `SaPasskeyLogin`              | Sign in with a passkey alone                                |
| `/verify-email-otp` | `SaVerifyOtp channel="email"` | Check an email code                                         |
| `/verify-phone-otp` | `SaVerifyOtp channel="phone"` | Check a text message code                                   |
| `/magic-link-sent`  | `SaMagicLinkSent`             | Wait for an emailed link to be used                         |
| `/verify-magiclink` | `SaVerifyMagicLink`           | Where the emailed link lands. The auth API builds this URL  |
| `/oauth/callback`   | `SaOAuthCallback`             | The OAuth redirect URI to register with your providers      |
| `/register-passkey` | `SaRegisterPasskey`           | Offer passkey enrolment after sign-up                       |

The screens navigate between those paths; pass `paths` to `createKitNavigator` if you mount them
elsewhere. The building blocks are exported too: `SaOtpInput` (bind it with `bind:value`),
`SaFallbackOptions`, `SaOAuthProviderButtons`, `SaAuthLayout`, and `authRoutePaths`.

The magic link and OAuth callback screens remove the token or code from the URL and from history once
they have read it, and will not send one a second time. Serve those routes with
`Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` (or `same-origin`) so the secret does not leave in a `Referer` before
then.

### Without SvelteKit

The screens never import a router. They navigate through an `AuthNavigator` set with
`setAuthNavigator`, so any router can drive them: implement its seven methods (`toScreen`, `toApp`,
`toLocation`, `state`, `query`, `dropQuery`, `absoluteUrl`) on top of your router.
`createKitNavigator` is the SvelteKit one.

### Styling

The screens render inside `.sa-auth` with plain `.sa-*` classes. The first screen to mount adds the
stylesheet to the top of `<head>`, so your own styles override it. Colors come from the same
`--seamless-*` custom properties the other bindings' screens read, so one theme covers every binding.
Under a Content Security Policy, pass `cspNonce`, or set `injectStyles: false` and link
`@seamless-auth/svelte/seamless-auth.css` yourself. The full token list is in the
[`@seamless-auth/react` README](https://github.com/fells-code/seamless-auth-react/tree/main/packages/react#theming-the-built-in-ui).

---

## Custom Screens

Every built-in screen is a thin view over a flow in `@seamless-auth/client`: `beginSignIn`,
`registerWithEmail`, `requestOtp` and `verifyOtp`, `watchMagicLink` and `finishMagicLinkSignIn`,
`startOAuthSignIn` and `completeOAuthCallback`, `enrollPasskey`, plus helpers such as
`loadLoginMethods`, `fallbackSignInOptions`, and `safeReturnPath`. A custom screen calls the same
flows, passing the session as its actions:

```ts
import { beginSignIn } from '@seamless-auth/client'

const step = await beginSignIn(auth, {
  identifier: email,
  passkeySupported: await auth.checkPasskeySupport(),
  configuredMethods: await auth.loadLoginMethods(),
})

if (step.kind === 'signed_in') await goto('/')
if (step.kind === 'choose_method') showOtherMethods(step.loginMethods)
if (step.kind === 'error') showError(step.message)
```

[How To Build Your Own Auth UI](/build/custom-auth-ui) walks through the flows in order. Its
examples use React hooks, but the client calls are the same.

---

## Server Rendering

The session is meant for the browser. On a server it does not read the session or browser storage,
the screens start no requests, and `requireAuth` redirects unless it was handed an `initialSession`.
If you do render on a server, create the session per request (never in a module shared between
requests) and pass `initialSession` from your adapter. Do not forward the browser's cookies to the
adapter's `/auth/users/me` from a server.
